page: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration belonging to the High Clock Speed family. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor operating at a base frequency of 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance allocates 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores utilizing hyper-threading, accompanied by a 25 MB L3 cache. It comes equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The server provides no integrated local disk storage, requiring external cloud block storage for persistence, and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps without bundled GPUs.

Performance across synthetic and compute benchmarks reflects its older Broadwell microarchitecture. The instance scored 1118.0 in Geekbench single-core and 2420.0 in multi-core tests, placing in the lower quartile of current server offerings. Similarly, PassMark testing shows a CPU score of 4187.36 and a memory score of 1546.68. Memory throughput shows limitations under heavy access, delivering 21.26 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 14.72 GB/sec on writes. However, single-threaded throughput shows acceptable capability in specific routines, such as gzip compression at 25.68 GB/sec and text processing in Geekbench at 1445.0.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.cm4.xlarge offers dedicated execution cores and steady clock rates without CPU credit throttling, making it predictable for baseline workloads. However, the lack of modern vector extensions such as AVX-512 and lower memory bandwidth reduce its compute density relative to contemporary architectures. It is primarily suitable for moderate, non-bursty background jobs, legacy enterprise applications, lightweight static web serving, and standard utility services that require a consistent clock frequency and a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio.

It features 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, 16.0 GB of memory, and 25 MB of L3 cache, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance includes no local storage, relying on external network-attached storage volumes, and has a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth with zero GPU acceleration. Benchmark measurements show moderate single-threaded execution, with 1118.0 in Geekbench single-core and a 4187.36 PassMark CPU score, alongside constrained memory bandwidth at 21.26 GB/sec for uncached reads. The hardware profile offers stable execution for legacy workloads, lightweight web servers, basic CI/CD runners, and general back-office enterprise tooling requiring fixed CPU allocations.
